draft.title: Shays' Rebellion
card: After the war, many farmers in western Massachusetts were in debt. Money was scarce, and state taxes and court orders forced some to lose their farms.
In 1786 and 1787, farmers led by Daniel Shays, a former Continental Army captain, shut courts and marched on a federal arsenal at Springfield. The state raised its own militia to end the revolt.
The national government could not help. It had no money to raise a strong army and no power to tax, so Massachusetts had to deal with the revolt on its own.
Many leaders feared more disorder. The revolt convinced them that the national government needed more power, which pushed them towards changing it.
draft.remember: A local revolt by indebted farmers showed that the national government was too weak to keep order.

a.q: Why did Shays' Rebellion alarm many American leaders about the national government?
opts: It showed the government could not deal with unrest
It showed the government was using too much power
It showed the states wanted to rejoin Britain
It showed the army had turned against the states
a.why: The national government had no power to tax and no money for a strong army, so Massachusetts had to put the revolt down itself. This made leaders fear disorder. The idea that the government held too much power is wrong, as the problem was its weakness.
a.clue: Think about who ended the revolt, and why.

b.q: Which statement best describes the effect of Shays' Rebellion?
opts: It pushed leaders to want a stronger national government
It pushed leaders to want a weaker national government
It led Massachusetts to cancel all debts owed by farmers
It forced the national government to end the state militias
b.why: Leaders feared more disorder and saw that a government without power to tax or raise an army could not protect order. This pushed them towards change. It did not lead them to weaken the government, because the revolt exposed weakness, not excess power.
b.clue: Ask what the revolt revealed about the national government.

a.best: It showed the government could not deal with unrest

b.best: It pushed leaders to want a stronger national government

problems.detail: Why (b) says the government had no power to 'raise an army'. The card says it had no money to raise a strong army. Under the Articles, Congress could call for troops but could not pay for them, so 'without power to raise an army' is inaccurate and contradicts the card's wording.
